chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man died during the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so the grave diggers came to him, but when they were with him, they could not dig anything. They complained about that to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, our iron does not work in the earth; it is as if we are striking it against rock.' He said: 'Why? If your companion was of good character, bring me a cup of water.' So they brought it to him. He put his hand into it, then sprinkled it upon the earth with a sprinkle, then said: 'Dig!' He said: 'So the grave diggers dug, and it was as if it were sand falling upon them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of good character in the ease of burial according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) demonstrates that 'husn al-khulq' (good character) has a tangible metaphysical impact on the physical world, causing the earth to yield easily for the righteous. This narrative is frequently cited by Shia scholars to illustrate the concept of 'taysir' (facilitation) in the grave, linking moral excellence directly to spiritual ease and divine favor.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man died during the era of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So the grave diggers came over, but when they were with him, they could not dig anything, and they complained of that to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saying, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Our irons (pick axes/spades) do not work in the ground. It is as if we are striking with it in the rock’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘If your (dead) companion was of good manners, come to me with a cup of water’. So they brought it to him<sup>saww</sup>. So he<sup>saww</sup> immersed his<sup>saww</sup> hand inside it, then sprinkled it upon the ground with a sprinkle, then said: ‘Dig!’. 
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So the grave-diggers dug, and it was as if it was sand falling upon them’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“During the time of the Holy Prophet a man died. The gravediggers could not dig a grave for him. They complained to the Messenger of Allah saying, ‘O Messenger of Allah, our picks do not work. It is as if we hit a rock.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Why it would be as such had your man been excellent in moral behavior. Bring to me a bowl of water.’ When water was brought he (the Messenger of Allah) (a.s.) immersed his hand into it and then sprinkled it on the ground. He then told them to dig. They began to dig and it was like sand falling fast upon them.”
